user.name=root, proc.pname=bash, proc.name/uid/tty null, and cmdline drawn from the
same three-command set "sudo -n systemctl status elastic-agent" / "sudo -n journalctl

(C-21d 3 rows, C-28d 13 rows, C-35d 10 rows), and the two same-millisecond triads at
06:41:01 and 06:41:41 mirror C-28d's 06:33:48/06:34:07 pair. The one column that could
separate them, falco.output_fields.container.id (ed96a85a7480, which most baseline
rows also carry), is listed in environment_notes as an unstable identifier that cannot
evidence a delta. The story's activity is Keycloak token requests over curl, which
produces no sudo events at all, so there is nothing for this lead to carry. The empty
projection asserts no change and invents nothing, matching the measurement's
delta_kind: absent; seq 0 being unreadable does not disturb this since it differs from
seq 1 only by adding proc.loginuid.
rows.evidence: The one readable query (seq 1) returns 6 rows, all with falco.output_fields.user.name=root, proc.pname=bash, proc.name/uid/tty null, and cmdline drawn from exactly the same three-command set seen in every control — "sudo -n systemctl status elastic-agent", "sudo -n journalctl -u elastic-agent -n 10", "sudo -n ss -tnlp" — emitted as two same-millisecond triads at 06:41:01 and 06:41:41. The live controls carry the identical triad with identical user/pname/cmdline values: C-21d 3 rows, C-35d 10 rows, C-28d 13 rows including near-adjacent bursts at 06:33:48 and 06:34:07 (19 s apart), so neither the command set nor the burst cadence is new, and 6 rows over 15 minutes is not above the 3–13 rows/hour control range. The only column that could separate observed from baseline is falco.output_fields.container.id (ed96a85a7480, matching most baseline rows anyway), and environment_notes lists that column as an unstable identifier that cannot evidence a delta. Seq 0 is unreadable, but it differs from seq 1 only by adding proc.loginuid, and seq 1 alone settles the lead.

carries no `@timestamp` bounds, and has no baseline-diff semantics — `measurement`
confirms `delta_kind: state-only`. The `observed` payload is `[]` (no CR rows, hence
no CR id, status, window, host scope, requester, or CHG-RUNNER prefix), and the
projection is likewise `[]`, correctly reporting no active change requests. There is
nothing for the oracle to distinguish and it invents nothing; the empty projection
matches the empty lookup result.

rows.form_notes: 26 projected event rows vs 30 observed dev.dana LOGIN_ERROR rows; per-event granularity only, no aggregate/loggerName rows
rows.rationale:
Observed seq 6 carries 30 LOGIN_ERROR rows for username `dev.dana` / client_id `admin-cli` from 172.18.0.6 in six bursts between 06:46:51.659Z and 06:47:20.670Z, and all three live controls (C-21d/C-28d/C-35d) for seq 0/1/2/6 return row_count 0 while seq 7 proves those windows were measured — so the delta is exactly this burst, on the non-unstable fields `username` and `client_id`. The projection emits that burst at the right granularity, with the correct user and clientId, six clusters in the right shape, and placeholders the IP, which is both story-ungrounded and on the unstable-identifier list.
The lead's heterogeneity is the successful-LOGIN half: seq 3 and seq 4 are row_count 0 in observed and in every control, so there is nothing for the projection to represent there, and it correctly emits no LOGIN rows — matching seq 0's `logins: 0, logouts: 0, refresh_tokens: 0`.
It also correctly omits the 06:13:33 `smoke.test` row and the extra loggerName values in seq 7, neither of which the story's activity produced. The 26-vs-30 count and the absence of an aggregate row are granularity divergences recorded in form_notes, not a misrepresented delta.
rows.evidence: Observed seq 0/1/2/6 carry 31 `org.keycloak.events` LOGIN_ERROR rows between 06:13:33.104Z and 06:47:20.670Z — 30 for username `dev.dana` / client_id `admin-cli` in six ~7-second bursts from 06:46:51 to 06:47:20, plus one `smoke.test` at 06:13:33 — while all three live controls (C-21d/C-28d/C-35d) return row_count 0 for the same queries; seq 7 confirms those control windows were measured and non-empty (4–5 rows of `org.keycloak.events.jpa.JpaEventStoreProvider`), so the zeros are real absence, not a dead stack. The distinguishing fields are `username` and `client_id` (dev.dana/admin-cli) and the LOGIN_ERROR counts, none of which are on the unstable-identifier list; ip_address 172.18.0.6 alone would not have counted. Queries disagree: seq 3 and seq 4 (successful LOGIN by ip/user/client, both the 06:55 and widened 07:00 bound) return row_count 0 in observed and in every control, i.e. `absent` — there is no successful-login half of the stuffing signature, and seq 0 records logins=0, logouts=0, refresh_tokens=0. Seq 7 additionally shows ten extra loggerName values in observed (io.quarkus, infinispan, exportimport) against a single logger in baseline, consistent with a stack start inside the window.

rows.rationale:
The rule-summary query (seq 3), untruncated on both sides, returns the same eleven falco.rule
values in the observed window as live control C-21d, with no cron, write-below-etc, or
authorized-keys rule present in either, and the targeted seq 2 query returns only the two rules
(Read sensitive file untrusted, Launch Sensitive Mount Container) that the controls also return.
In the untruncated seq 1 payload every (rule, proc, parent) tuple — including Drop and
execute/openssl/sh, Launch Suspicious Network Tool/nc/runuser and Ingress/curl/bash in
2c1e2ec93d17 — has a counterpart in C-21d; only falco.output_fields.container.id groupings and
raw counts differ, and environment_notes marks container ids as regenerated per lever-up while the
controls' own counts swing wider (Read sensitive file untrusted 9 / 0 / 36 across controls) than
the observed 54. The story's curl loop against keycloak produces no categorical field these
queries surface that the baseline lacks, so an empty projection asserting no delta matches the
measurement of record.
